Synopsis:
UK CPI rose to 2.9% in July 2026 (in line with Reuters consensus, slightly above BoE's 2.8% forecast), keeping GBP/USD supported at $1.3552. Markets price at least one BoE rate hike this year, but a Reuters economist poll majority expects rates held at 3.75%. Goldman Sachs flags this divergence as a likely sterling headwind. Elevated oil prices (driven by stalled US-Iran negotiations) add a macro drag. Domestically generated inflation remains contained; Capital Economics sees CPI returning to 2.0% by end-2027.
